cues: There is a desert in the south of Arabia that the people who lived near it called the Empty Quarter.
The old storytellers said why.
When the world was divided, two parts went to the children of Adam.
One went to the wild people beyond the mountains, and the fourth was left with nothing in it.
They called it Rubʿ al Khali.
It is the largest continuous sand desert on earth.
About 250 000 square miles larger than all of france more than 600 miles long and 300 miles
Wide dunes standing 800 feet from base to crest sand that is not is not yellow but red gold and
At dawn and dusk the whole desert glows with iron in it in summer the heat climbs past 120 degrees
In some years no rain falls at all but it was not always empty
Dig into the hard pan between the dunes and you find the floors of ancient lakes
And the bones of hippopotamus and water buffalo that grazed there when the deserts
Was green then the rains move the way when rains move the way they are moving again in our time
And the people who stayed did not flee it they learned it the bedouin raised their camels along
The edges of that sand for centuries and learned its wells and its stars and its winds the way you
Learn the moods of someone you will live beside your whole life and there was a man one of the
Alas, Alas, who walked into the middle of it, and did not hurry.
He did not simply wake one morning and go.
The crossing was not made out of the sand it was made before,
In the quiet days, in the quiet years, when no one was watching.
He ate light and clean. He gathered his water and salt.
He went to the elders and laid before them what he had seen,
And they waited for days against a crossing of men long gone,
And over and over he ran the whole crossing behind his closed eyes,
Every dune field, every well, Until his body knew the country before his feet touched it, a grain of it.
He walked with a small pebble in his fist, river-worn and smooth,
And pictured it resting on his tongue, And the picturing alone brought water back to his dry mouth.
He counted his breath to his stride, four in, hold four, six out, hold.
On the soft dune faces he leaned from the ankles, never the waist, chest open, the way a tree stands into the wind.
He carried no mat, he was the mat.
By night he read the stars, by day the sun, and when the dust storms came he read the sand itself.
Because the great dunes lie at the same angle to the wind that built them.
And there was an inner training deeper than the lakes he was taught from a child to carry home
Inside himself so he never ate for it on the long crossing he was taught to go still
And sit with the ones who came before him so he was never truly alone he was taught the words that
Steady a shaking body I am safe I am calm my mind is quiet the power i was born with is still mine
And he was taught to laugh, even out there, especially out there.
On the fourth day, the well was dry.
The far well, the one his whole crossing was strung upon, was cracked mud.
And the frightened man at that moment does the one thing that ends his crossing.
His heart bolts.
He drinks his last water too fast or runs into the heat.
And all his water pours out through his skin into the sand.
At that moment, the fear says run.
And out there, the fear is always wrong.
So he did the hard, disciplined thing, the trained thing.
He sat down in the shade of the dune.
He softened his eyes to the whole horizon.
He counted his breath, four in, hold four, six out, hold four.
He let the fear stand beside him and gave it no chair to sit in.
And when his heart rate came down, his quiet mind remembered a seep his grandfather had told him about once, and only once, half a day back and to the north.
Running only in the years, the great rains fail everywhere else.
This kind of year. He got up. He went north. The seep was there, and he laughed when he found it.
He stood over that small trickle of brown water in the middle of the largest emptiness on earth
And laughed. He drank. He filled his skin. He rested until the sun went down, and then he went
On, and he crossed. You do not make the calm out there. You retrieve it. You store it in your bones,
The quiet days before this week store some of that quiet each morning before the day can set your
State for you hold your pebble or picture it say the words I am safe I am calm my mind is quiet
The power I was born with is still mine then breathe in for four hold for four out for six
Hold for four, five times, and find one thing to laugh about.
